name: TeamStarWolf - Kevin Mitnick Intrusions Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK techniques that the verified record of Kevin Mitnick's intrusions and the two Mitnick and Simon books supports: the 1999 DOJ plea record, Mitnick's 2000 Senate testimony, Shimomura's January 1995 technical account of the Christmas Day 1994 intrusion, DOJ records for two Art of Intrusion stories, and CISA AA23-320A and HHS HC3 for the modern help desk comparison. Revoked ids map through data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/MITNICK_INTRUSIONS.md. Scores rank the record, not the mapping: 100 is conduct Mitnick admitted in the plea or described in testimony, 75 is the 1994 intrusion whose attacker the primary record does not name, 50 is an Art of Intrusion story with a DOJ record, 25 is the modern comparison only. Except where AA23-320A or HC3 cite an id, the mappings are this study's reading.

techniques.comment: Impersonation: the 1999 plea record (impersonating Nokia Mobile Phones employees; De Payne posing as a Nokia employee) [1]; Mitnick's testimony on posing as a fellow employee to IRS and SSA staff [4][5]. Revoked T1656 maps here via data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl [35][26]. Modern comparison: AA23-320A cites T1656 for Scattered Spider [24]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/MITNICK_INTRUSIONS.md.

Pretext phone calls: testimony on finding modem numbers by social engineering and on the Motorola firmware calls [4][5]; plea admission of social engineering [1]. Modern comparison: AA23-320A cites the id [24]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/MITNICK_INTRUSIONS.md.
